newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares firm 0.79 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares firm 0.79 pct to new record.

text.p: The Istanbul stock market index continued its string of records by ending firmer on Monday, following a confidence vote won in parliament on Saturday by Turkey's new right-left coalition government.
The IMKB National-100 closed at a new all-time high of 2,043, up 16 points, or 0.79 percent from Friday's previous record of 2,027.

"Sales followed a strong opening because positive expectations were already priced in ahead of the vote. But activity led by state shares boosted the market again in the afternoon," said Oya Ozturk from Vakif securities.

The market index has rallied 30.5 percent and hit 10 record closes since June 18 when the former Islamist-led coalition government resigned and hopes flared that it would be replaced by a secularist alliance.
Daily trade volume rose 20.2 percent to 37.64 trillion lira ($245.4 million) from Friday's 31.31 trillion ($206.9 million).
"Better turnover is an indication of liquidity influx to the bourse. I expect activity in state shares to persist tomorrow. The uptrend is likely to continue smoothly," Ozturk said.
"Concrete implementations by the new government, such as progress in privatisation will support the uptrend," she added.
